status: declared by the pull request that closes #965 before any number was computed; a measurement, not a record. Nothing is published: no published declaration, no record in docs/runs/ and no decided value changes, nothing after 2025-12-31 is scored, and no lockbox day is read. The tax-date definition is a data meaning and adopting it for B2 or for H8's calendar is a section 13 question: both are Eleonora's (#965, criterion 3). Development data, never a verdict (scoring protocol v1, #640)
hypothesis: H5 step 2 (B2's day-type pools), H6 step 1 (the risk-date set) and H8 (the calendar ranker)
ruling: Eleonora, 19 October 2026, relayed on #958 (five-lens review, next-in-line, Lens A)
why: tax_date marks the 15th of the months 4, 6, 9 and 12 (data.TAX_DEADLINE_MONTHS). 15 October is the extended corporate and individual filing deadline, a mid-month coupon settlement and the first settlement of Treasury's fiscal year; in 2019 and 2025 the spread printed +20, +25 and +14 bp on 2019-10-15, 2019-10-16 and 2025-10-15, on days where tax_date reads 0

alternative.module: repo_model.tax_date_october; each label is a function of the date and metadata/market_holidays.json
alternative.october: the 15th of October rolled forward off weekends and DC holidays (the rule of data.corporate_tax_deadline) and the two market days after it (the count of data.tax_date_market_days): a day the declared types call ordinary becomes tax_date inside it. The published tax_date column is not changed, so the alternative differs from the as-is B2 only in October; the market-day count of #538 and the DC-day count of the published column agree in October (Columbus Day is 8-14 October)
alternative.precedence: quarter_end and month_end keep their precedence over tax_date, as in the declared reporting_day_type; 15 October is never either
alternative.control: the coupon effect: the 15th of the months 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 11 (neither a published tax month nor October) rolled forward on the market calendar, with the two market days after it, relabelled tax_date in the same way. The same shape as the October window, in months with no tax deadline. A calendar rule, so that every label is known ahead of its date as B2's target labels must be; the share of control deadlines on which the panel's treasury_settlement_coupons column is positive is reported beside it

scored_days.decision_days: every business day of the published panel on which every forecast of the comparison builds and whose five targets (h = 1..5 business days later on the panel's calendar) all fall on or before 2025-12-31; for the ranker (b) the 20 targets (h = 1..20) all fall on or before 2025-12-31. A decision day on which B2 as is or B2 with an alternative has no sample of a lead's type in the trailing year is dropped from every model of the comparison and counted
scored_days.lockbox: the script calls lockbox.require_unlocked on every decision and target day and refuses a day after 2025-12-31
scored_days.panel: the published panel (tests/fixtures/snapshots/funding_inputs built at cutoff 2026-09-08T21:31:42+00:00, digest in metadata/funding_panel_manifest.json)

a.label: B2 with the alternative tax_date against B2 as is
a.candidate: protocol_benchmarks.b2_forecast with splits = AlternativeLabels(declared splits, which=...), unchanged otherwise
a.benchmark: protocol_benchmarks.b2_forecast with the declared splits, unchanged
a.reference: B1 (protocol_benchmarks.b1_forecast) against B2 as is and against each alternative, to put the size of the change beside the gap B2 has to B1
a.scores: grid_crps (primary) and upper_tail_twcrps (key secondary), each the mean over a decision day's leads

b.label: H8's calendar ranker with the alternative's window in its set, against the calendar ranker as is
b.candidate: ranking.calendar with a lead also flagged where tax_date_october.extra_risk_flag(target day, which) holds
b.benchmark: ranking.calendar as is (a quarter-end, a tax date, or a coupon settlement where it was public at the decision instant), ties broken by date
b.metrics: precision@3, precision@5 over all windows and recall@3, recall@5 over the windows with a pressure day (ranking_694.json), pressure the whole-basis-point event strictly above +5 bp (ranking.realised)
b.interval: the percentile interval of ranking_694.paired (stationary bootstrap, mean block 20, 10,000 draws, seed 965); the studentized scorer is used where it is defined

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.pairing: each candidate against its benchmark on the same decision days, skill = mean(d) / mean(S(benchmark)) with d = S(benchmark) - S(candidate): positive favours the candidate
scoring.interval: scoring_protocol.paired_test, the studentized stationary bootstrap of ruling 1 (#739): mean block 10, 10,000 draws, seed 965; the 90% two-sided interval is the 5th to 95th studentized bound, for mean(d) and for skill
scoring.outcomes: the panel's spread_bps at the target day, as #686, #693 and #959 read it

splits.regime: SplitDeclaration.regime of the decision day (metadata/evaluation_splits.json): 2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024 and 2025-26 (the last is scored to 2025-12-31 only)
splits.target: the target day's window: 'target: october window' (the October window alone: its count of target days is reported), 'target: control window' (the control months), 'target: tax_date as is' (the published tax types), and 'target: other days'. A decision day's score in a target group is the mean over the leads whose target is in it
splits.ranker: the windows that contain an October window day among their 20 targets, the windows that contain a control day, and the rest, beside the pooled and regime rows
splits.minimum: a group of fewer than 20 decision days is listed with its means and is not tested

reading_rules.a: the alternative is better than B2 as is on a group when the 90% interval of its skill against B2 as is lies above zero, worse when it lies below; otherwise the group shows no difference. A gain that appears in the October window and also in the control's own window is the coupon effect and not a tax-date effect; a gain in the October window alone is the expected place for the October label and is read as such. The control is read on its own window the same way
reading_rules.b: read the same way against the calendar ranker as is, on the October windows and on the control windows
reading_rules.no_verdict: every sentence on the page says development data, not a verdict

limits.published: no published declaration and no docs/runs/ record changes; the B2 of scoring protocol v1, H8's declaration (#694) and the published tax_date are only read
limits.walk_time: B2 and the ranker's calendar need no refit; if the run is expected to take more than about two hours it follows the needs-mac rule on #46
questions_for_eleonora: adopt 15 October in the tax_date definition (a data meaning), for B2 and so for scoring protocol v1's B2 and its section 13, and for H8's calendar?
whether the coupon-effect control, if it matches the October result, means the label should be a coupon-settlement label and not a tax-date label
